source.title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization

accepted.question_text: Let S be a finite set of line segments in R^d. Suppose that for every two distinct segments s' and s'' in S, there exist two distinct parallel supporting hyperplanes H' and H'' of the convex hull of the union of all segments in S such that s' lies in H' and s'' lies in H''. Must the number of segments satisfy |S| <= 2^(d-1)?

evidence.quote: Question 1. Suppose S is a set of segments in Rd such that for every s0, s00 in S with s0 not equal s00 there are different parallel supporting hyperplanes H0, H00 of the convex hull of the union of the segments, such that s0 lies in H0 and s00 lies in H00. Then is it true that |S| <= 2d-1?

accepted.question_text: Let S_k be a finite set of k-simplices in R^d, with 1 <= k <= d - 2. Suppose S_k satisfies the same antipodal-support property as in the segment problem: for every two distinct simplices, there are distinct parallel supporting hyperplanes of the convex hull of the union of all simplices in S_k, with one simplex contained in one supporting hyperplane and the other contained in the other. Must |S_k| <= 2^(d-k)?

evidence.quote: Of course, more generally, we may consider a set Sk of k-simplices in Rd, which satisfy the word-for-word analogue of the above property. Is it true, that then |Sk| <= 2d-k? Here 1 <= k <= d - 2.

accepted.question_text: In d-dimensional Euclidean space E^d, a plank is a closed region bounded by two parallel hyperplanes, and its width is the distance between those boundary hyperplanes. Given a family of planks whose total width is smaller than 2, what is the maximum possible volume of the subset of the unit ball in E^d that is covered by the planks?
accepted.context_brief: Plank coverage of a unit ball

evidence.quote: A plank is a closed region of the d-dimensional Euclidean space Ed bounded by a pair of parallel hyperplanes. The width of a plank is the distance between its boundary hyperplanes. Question 2. Given a family of planks whose sum of widths is smaller than 2, what is the maximum volume of the part of the unit ball in Ed that can be covered by the planks?

accepted.question_text: Let S^d be the d-dimensional unit sphere in E^(d+1), with d >= 2. A spherically convex body is a closed spherically convex subset of S^d with interior points that lies in a closed hemisphere, equivalently the intersection of S^d with a proper closed convex cone in E^(d+1). Its inradius r(K) is the spherical radius of the largest spherical ball contained in K. If spherically convex bodies K_1,...,K_n cover a spherical ball B of radius r(B) < pi/2 in S^d, must sum_{i=1}^n r(K_i) >= r(B)?

evidence.quote: Recall that Sd stands for the d-dimensional unit sphere in (d+1)-dimensional Euclidean space Ed+1; d >= 2. A spherically convex body is a closed, spherically convex subset K of Sd with interior points and lying in some closed hemisphere. The inradius r(K) of K is the spherical radius of the largest spherical ball contained in K. Question 3. Let the spherically convex bodies K1,...,Kn cover the spherical ball B of radius r(B) < pi/2 in Sd; d >= 2. Then prove or disprove that sum r(Ki) >= r(B).

accepted.question_text: Let n points in three-dimensional space be in general position and be obtained by a small perturbation of a sqrt(n) by sqrt(n) grid. Is every triangulation of that point set bounded by O(n^(3/2)) simplices?

evidence.quote: Question 4. Is it true that for each set of points in general position that results from an sqrt(n) x sqrt(n) grid in three-dimensional space by a small perturbation, every triangulation of the set consists of at most O(n3/2) simplices?

accepted.question_text: For a simple arrangement A_{d,n} of n hyperplanes in dimension d, where any d hyperplanes intersect at a distinct point, call the d-dimensional polyhedra defined by the hyperplanes the cells and call the bounded facets of an unbounded cell external. Let Phi_A(d,n) be the minimum number of external facets over all simple arrangements defined by n hyperplanes in dimension d. For n > d >= 3, is Phi_A(d,n+1) >= Phi_A(d,n) + Phi_A(d-1,n), and in dimension 3 is equality attained as Phi_A(3,n) = n^2 - 3n + 4 for all n >= 6?

evidence.quote: An arrangement A d,n of n hyperplanes in dimension d is simple if any d hyperplanes intersect at a distinct point. The d-dimensional polyhedra defined by the hyperplanes of an arrangement A d,n are called the cells of A d,n. The bounded facets of an unbounded cell are called external. Let Phi_A(d,n) be the minimum number of external facets for any simple arrangement defined by n hyperplanes in dimension d.

Question 5. We hypothesize that Phi_A(d,n+1) >= Phi_A(d,n) + Phi_A(d-1,n) for n > d >= 3, and that the inequality is satisfied with equality for d = 3 and n >= 6, i.e., Phi_A(3,n) = n2 - 3n + 4 for n >= 6.

accepted.question_text: In spherical space S^d and hyperbolic space H^d, for a fixed ball and a variable simplex of prescribed volume V, is the volume of the intersection of the ball and the simplex maximized when the simplex is regular and concentric with the ball?

evidence.quote: The maximum volume of the intersection of a fixed ball in Ed and a variable simplex of given volume V is attained when the simplex is regular and concentric with the ball. Question 6. Show that the above statement holds true in spherical and hyperbolic space as well.

accepted.question_text: For n >= 3, determine q(n), the minimum number of cubes in R^n, each with edge length smaller than 1 and not necessarily parallel to the covered cube, whose union contains a unit cube.
accepted.context_brief: Covering a unit cube by smaller cubes

evidence.quote: Question 7. What is the minimum number q(n) of cubes in Rn of edge length smaller than 1 whose union contains a unit cube?
It is not difficult to prove that q(2) = 3 and that q(n) >= n + 1 for every n, but the exact value of q(n) has not yet been established for any n >= 3.

accepted.question_text: For n >= 2, let the Boolean Quadric Polytope P_n be the convex hull, in dimension d = n(n+1)/2, of the 0/1 solutions to x_i x_j = y_ij for all i < j in N = {1,2,...,n}. Find a formula or strong bounds for the d-dimensional volume of P_n.

evidence.quote: Question 8. For n >= 2, the Boolean Quadric Polytope Pn is the convex hull in dimension d = n(n+1)/2 of the 0/1 solutions to xi xj = yij for all i < j in N := {1,2,...,n}. Give a formula or good bounds for the d-dimensional volume of Pn.

accepted.question_text: For n >= 3, geometrically characterize the n-simplices in Euclidean n-space E^n whose incenter lies on their Euler line, where the Euler line for such a simplex is the affine hull of its circumcenter and centroid.
accepted.context_brief: Incenters on Euler lines of simplices

evidence.quote: Question 9. Characterize geometrically those n-simplices in En, n >= 3, for which the incenter lies on the Euler line.
No analogous characterization is known for n-simplices in En (n >= 3) whose incenter I lies on their Euler line, which still is the affine hull of C and S.

accepted.question_text: Let r >= 2 and N >= 1 be integers, with N allowed to be sufficiently large as a function of r. Suppose r(N+1) points P_{ij} in R^N are indexed by 1 <= i <= r and 1 <= j <= N+1, and suppose 0 belongs to conv{P_{1j},...,P_{rj}} for every j. Suppose further that {1,2,...,N+1} is partitioned into color classes C_1,...,C_m with |C_k| <= r-1 for every k. Must there exist choices k_1,...,k_{N+1} in {1,...,r} such that 0 belongs to conv{P_{k_1,1},...,P_{k_{N+1},N+1}} and, whenever a and b are distinct indices in the same color class C_k, the selected labels satisfy k_a != k_b?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. (A Multicolored Caratheodory Conjecture). Let r >= 2 and N >= 1 be integers. Suppose we are given r(N+1) points Pij in RN that are indexed by 1 <= i <= r and 1 <= j <= N+1. Assume that 0 is in conv{P1j,...,Prj} for all 1 <= j <= N+1. Assume further that the index set {1,2,...,N+1} is partitioned as C1 union ... union Cm such that all color classes are small: |Ck| <= r - 1. Then there exist k1,...,kN+1 in {1,...,r} such that 0 is in conv{Pk1,1,...,PkN+1,N+1} and for any two distinct a,b in the same color class Ck we have ka != kb.

accepted.question_text: Let K be a compact convex set in R^n, and let n_1,...,n_s be positive integers with n_1 + ... + n_s = n + 1. For every point z in K, do there exist non-empty faces F_1,...,F_s of K such that z lies in conv(F_1 union ... union F_s) and dim(F_i) <= n_i - 1 for every i = 1,...,s?
accepted.context_brief: Face decomposition of compact convex sets

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. If K is a compact convex set in Rn and n1,...,ns are positive integers with n1 + ... + ns = n + 1, then, for every point z in K, non-empty faces F1,...,Fs of K exist such that z is in conv(F1 union ... union Fs) and dim Fi <= ni - 1 for all i = 1,...,s.

accepted.question_text: For a positive integer n >= 2, let C(n) be the maximum number of touching pairs among packings of n congruent unit balls in Euclidean 3-space E^3. For which n can C(n) be achieved by a packing of n unit balls consisting of parallel layers, where each layer is a subset of the densest infinite hexagonal layer of unit balls?

evidence.quote: For a given positive integer n >= 2 find the largest number C(n) of touching pairs in a packing of n congruent balls in E3. Problem 1. Find those positive integers n for which C(n) can be achieved in a packing of n unit balls in E3 consisting of parallel layers of unit balls each being a subset of the densest infinite hexagonal layer of unit balls.

accepted.question_text: For the contact-number function C(n), the maximum number of touching pairs in a packing of n unit balls in E^3, determine rigorously whether the lower bounds C(10) >= 25, C(11) >= 29, C(12) >= 33, and C(13) >= 36 are exact equalities.
accepted.context_brief: Exact small contact numbers in E^3

evidence.quote: Finally, if we take the 12 vertices of a cuboctahedron of edge length 2 in E3 along with its center of symmetry, then the 13 unit balls centered about them have 36 contacts implying that C(13) >= 36. Whether in any of the inequalities C(10) >= 25, C(11) >= 29, C(12) >= 33, and C(13) >= 36 we have equality seems to be an open question.
The main results are: C(9) = 21; C(10) = 25 and C(11) = 29. However, the status of the mathematical rigour of the approaches remains to be seen.

accepted.question_text: Let C(n) be the maximum number of touching pairs in a packing of n unit balls in Euclidean 3-space. Does the limit as n tends to infinity of (6n - C(n)) / n^(2/3) exist?

evidence.quote: If P is a packing of n unit balls in E3, then let C(P) stand for the number of touching pairs in P, that is, let C(P) denote the number of edges of the contact graph of P and call it the contact number of P. Moreover, let C(n) be the largest C(P) for packings P of n unit balls in E3.
Problem 2. Does the limit lim n to infinity (6n - C(n)) / n2/3 exist?

accepted.question_text: For a graph G, let ed(G) be the smallest integer k >= 1 such that every assignment of vectors p_1,...,p_n admits vectors q_1,...,q_n in R^k preserving the squared distances on all edges of G. Let the suspension of G be the graph obtained by adding one new vertex adjacent to every vertex of G. Is ed(suspension(G)) <= ed(G) + 1, equivalently ed(suspension(G)) = ed(G) + 1 given the known reverse inequality?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Determine the validity of the inequality ed(suspension G) <= ed(G) + 1, relating the Euclidean dimension of a graph G and of its suspension.

Given a graph G, its Euclidean dimension is the graph parameter ed(G) which is defined as the smallest integer k >= 1 such that, for every family of vectors p1,...,pn, there exists another family of vectors q1,...,qn in Rk satisfying squared edge distances. The suspension graph is obtained from G by adding to it a new node and making it adjacent to all the nodes of G.
Thus our first problem asks whether the converse inequality holds or, equivalently, whether it is true that ed(suspension G) = ed(G) + 1.

accepted.question_text: For a graph G, let gd(G) be the Gram dimension: the smallest integer k >= 1 such that every vector family p_1,...,p_n admits vectors q_1,...,q_n in R^k preserving all vertex squared norms and all inner products on edges. Let nu_equal(G) be the van der Holst parameter defined as the maximum corank of a positive semidefinite matrix M in the cone C(G) of matrices with zero entries on nonedges, subject to the Strong Arnold Property. Is gd(G) <= nu_equal(G), so that gd(G) and nu_equal(G) coincide given the known inequality gd(G) >= nu_equal(G)?
accepted.context_brief: Gram dimension and van der Holst parameter

evidence.quote: The Gram dimension gd(G) is defined as the smallest integer k >= 1 such that, for every family of vectors p1,...,pn, there exists another family of vectors q1,...,qn in Rk satisfying squared norms and edge inner products.
Problem 4. Determine the validity of the inequality gd(G) <= nu_equal(G), relating the Gram dimension gd(G) and the van der Holst parameter nu_equal(G).
The parameter nu_equal(G) is defined as the maximum corank of a matrix M in C(G) satisfying the Strong Arnold Property.
Our second problem asks for the validity of the converse inequality. In other words, is it true that the two graph parameters gd(.) and nu_equal(.) coincide?

accepted.question_text: In fixed-dimensional localization, one seeks positions of n points in a target Euclidean dimension d from a subset of pairwise distances, equivalently through a rank-constrained semidefinite program find Z with E(Z)=u, Z positive semidefinite, and rank(Z) <= d. Ji, Sze, Zhou, So, and Ye propose a non-convex Schatten p-quasi-norm regularization and a potential reduction algorithm that can localize universally rigid instances and some globally rigid but not universally rigid instances. Which input instances can this potential reduction algorithm localize in the required dimension?

evidence.quote: Determining the positions of a set of n points in Euclidean space based on knowledge of a subset of the pairwise distances is a fundamental geometric problem. Such a fixed-dimensional localization problem can be formulated as a rank-constrained semidefinite program: find Z such that E(Z)=u, Z is positive semidefinite, and rank(Z) <= d.

The value (fp(Z))1/p is known as the Schatten p-quasi-norm of Z. Ji et al. design a potential reduction algorithm and show that it can approximate a first-order critical point of Problem (9) to any given accuracy in polynomial time.

Problem 5. One of the most immediate questions is to understand the power of the non-convex Schatten quasi-norm regularization in the context of localization. Specifically, can we characterize the class of input instances that can be localized in the required dimension by the potential reduction algorithm of Ji et al.?

accepted.question_text: For the non-convex Schatten p-quasi-norm regularization approach to fixed-dimensional localization, what rigidity-theoretic meaning does the dual vector y in the first-order critical point conditions have? More specifically, do rigidity-theoretic results that interpret semidefinite-programming dual variables as edge stresses satisfying equilibrium conditions have counterparts in the Schatten quasi-norm regularization setting?
accepted.context_brief: Rigidity meaning of Schatten dual variables

evidence.quote: Along the same direction, it will be interesting to study the rigidity-theoretic implications of Schatten quasi-norm regularization. A starting point could be to understand the rigidity-theoretic interpretations of the dual vector y in the definition of the first-order critical point.

So and Ye state that each dual variable in the SDP relaxation corresponds to a stress on an edge of the input graph, and the optimality conditions correspond to a certain equilibrium condition on the input graph. A natural question would be whether these results have counterparts in the Schatten quasi-norm regularization setting.
